subject: Help with syntax for regressons of nonlinear latent variable

messages.author: 59a514fef8934fc5
messages.subject: Help with syntax for regressons of nonlinear latent variable
parts:
Dear all,
Please can someone check my syntax - I imagine I'm close but the model doesn't run.
I am trying to predict (using regression) a latent outcome variable from a latent predictor variable (I have done this in SPSS; this analysis is designed to model variables as latent variables in order to remove measurement error). I am trying to test for nonlinear effects, comparing 3 models that have indicators that respectively consist of (1) the raw item scores, (2) squared item scores, and (3) cubed item scores. I would like to compare the fit of the 3 models, akin to something like R squared change. I understand that there is no need to define covariances between latent variables as "all exogenous latent variables are correlated by default" in Lavaan. My syntax is below. Any help would be really appreciated!!

library(foreign)

STAI <- read.dta("c:/Users/Laptop/Desktop/Hawaiianfile.dta")

 

library(lavaan)

model <- '

# latent variable definitions

STAI =~ trait1 + trait2 + trait3 + trait4 + trait5 + trait6 + trait7 + trait8 + trait9 + trait10 + trait11 + trait12 + trait13 + trait14 + trait15 + trait16 + trait17 + trait18 + trait19 + trait20

STAISQUARED =~ trait1SQUARED + trait2SQUARED + trait3SQUARED + trait4SQUARED + trait5SQUARED + trait6SQUARED + trait7SQUARED + trait8SQUARED + trait9SQUARED + trait10SQUARED + trait11SQUARED + trait12SQUARED + trait13SQUARED + trait14SQUARED + trait15SQUARED + trait16SQUARED + trait17SQUARED + trait18SQUARED + trait19SQUARED + trait20SQUARED

STAICUBED =~ trait1CUBED + trait2CUBED + trait3CUBED + trait4CUBED + trait5CUBED + trait6CUBED + trait7CUBED + trait8CUBED + trait9CUBED + trait10CUBED + trait11CUBED + trait12CUBED + trait13CUBED + trait14CUBED + trait15CUBED + trait16CUBED + trait17CUBED + trait18CUBED + trait19CUBED + trait20CUBED

CESD =~ dep_1 + dep_2 + dep_3 + dep_4 + dep_5 + dep_6 + dep_7 + dep_8 + dep_9 + dep_10 + dep_11 + dep_12 + dep_13 + dep_14 + dep_15 + dep_16 + dep_17 + dep_18 + dep_19 + dep_20’

 

# regressions

CESD ~ STAI + STAISQUARED + STAICUBED

 

fit <- sem(model, data = STAI)

summary(fit, standardized = TRUE, fit.measures = TRUE)

messages.author: 0325c6a976085eab
messages.subject: Re: Help with syntax for regressons of nonlinear latent variable
parts:
Can you explain what you mean by "the model doesn't run."

I think your problem might be this. Consider just this:
STAI =~ trait1 + trait2
STAISQUARED =~ trait1SQUARED + trait2SQUARED
STAICUBED =~ trait1CUBED + trait2CUBED

According to the model, the only reason that trait1, trait1sq and trait1cu correlate is because the latent variables they indicate are correlated. But variables tend to be (very) highly correlated with their square and cube so this model is likely very badly misspecified.

jeremy

messages.subject: Re: Help with syntax for regressons of nonlinear latent variable
parts: In the word file, the closing quote mark is not a regular ' but is a 'smart quote' - ’ (and you have to look *very* closely to see the difference). If that's what you are running in R, that might be the source of the error. But it might be that Word has changed the quote after you pasted it. It's better to send code in text files, because of that issue.

On 25 May 2016, at 18:13, Jeremy Miles <jeremy...@gmail.com> wrote:

 Can you explain what you mean by "the model doesn't run."

I think your problem might be this. Consider just this:

STAI =~ trait1 + trait2
STAISQUARED =~ trait1SQUARED + trait2SQUARED
STAICUBED =~ trait1CUBED + trait2CUBED

According to the model, the only reason that trait1, trait1sq and trait1cu correlate is because the latent variables they indicate are correlated. But variables tend to be (very) highly correlated with their square and cube so this model is likely very badly misspecified.

jeremy

messages.subject: Re: Help with syntax for regressons of nonlinear latent variable
parts: I think I used regular speech marks (I have successfully run CFA and SEM before in R, I'm just having problems with this). See attached.
Looks like you are closing your quotation mark (i.e., ending the model syntax) before you include the regression lines:

# regressions
CESD ~ STAI + STAISQUARED + STAICUBED
CESD ~ STAI + STAISQUARED + STAICUBED

I'm not sure why you have the same thing in black and red, but don't include redundant specifications in the syntax; it might throw an error saying you specified the same parameter(s) twice.

summary(fit)
Error in summary(fit) :
error in evaluating the argument 'object' in selecting a method for function 'summary': Error:
object 'fit' not found

The error says you tried to get a summary from "fit" before you created "fit".  Same problem when you run inspect(fit, "cov.lv") -- it looks like your lavaan object is "fit1", not "fit".
